beats.narration_slice: Disney's earliest Kansas City cartoons were the Laugh-O-Grams.
beats.visual: A small early-1920s Kansas City animation workspace rendered as a vertical retro educational illustration: wooden drawing desk, pinned animation sheets showing simple fairy-tale-style cartoon figures, ink bottle, pencils, registration pegs, and a modest film camera stand, all on warm aged paper with loose sepia ink contours and restrained wash; no readable lettering.
beats.purpose: Establish the Laugh-O-Grams as Disney's earliest Kansas City cartoon work and place them in a modest period animation studio.
beats.continuity: First body image transitions from the opened history book into its illustrated early-1920s Kansas City animation world.

beats.visual: A vertical visual timeline metaphor without labels: at the lower foreground, rough early cartoon animation sheets and a hand-cranked film reel; farther upward and noticeably separated in time, only a distant generic round-eared mouse-like silhouette is hinted at behind several intervening calendar-page shapes, kept abstract and secondary so it does not imply the mouse came first.
beats.purpose: Show that the Laugh-O-Grams preceded the famous mouse era by several years.
beats.continuity: Keeps the same aged-paper ink world while pulling back from the studio desk into a simple passage-of-time composition.

beats.visual: An early-1920s film set and drawing table sharing one simple vertical composition: a young live-action girl figure suggested in period dress near a plain camera setup, with loose hand-drawn cartoon animals emerging from animation sheets beside her; warm cream paper, sepia ink, muted ochre and faded teal accents, no text.
beats.purpose: Introduce the Alice Comedies as the next major step after the Laugh-O-Grams.
beats.continuity: Moves forward chronologically while retaining the same period studio materials and hand-drawn visual language.

beats.narration_slice: Those blended live action with animation.
beats.visual: A single integrated scene showing a period live-action girl standing on a simple photographed floor while hand-drawn ink characters and sketched props appear to interact around her, with the boundary between filmed reality and drawn animation visibly merging through loose ink strokes rather than split panels.
beats.purpose: Explain the defining Alice Comedies technique of combining filmed live action with drawn animation.
beats.continuity: Pushes closer into the Alice Comedies concept introduced in the previous beat, now emphasizing the mixed-media interaction itself.

beats.narration_slice: Steamboat Willie was a milestone, not the start.
beats.visual: A chronological depth composition in the same 1920s ink style: foreground contains earlier worn animation sheets, ink bottles, and film reels; farther along the visual path sits a later simple river-steamboat cinema motif illuminated like an important milestone, but clearly positioned after the earlier materials, with no branded characters or readable title text.
beats.purpose: Clarify that Steamboat Willie was historically important but came after Disney's earlier animation work.
beats.continuity: Concludes the chronological sequence by placing the later steamboat milestone beyond the previously established Kansas City and Alice-era materials.
